name: abandoned rusted car facing south seen from above: trunk, roof and hood tops with cracked glass, front grille and bumper below
label: wasteland_ruins/car-rust-v

answer.evidence: Rows 0-29 show the horizontal surfaces of the car. The trunk (rows 0-7) ends in a light edge line at row 8. The roof and glass (rows 9-19) end at the dark line at row 20. The hood (rows 21-26) ends in a light edge line at row 26 and is followed by darker shadow rows 27-29. Below that is a vertical front face of about 15 rows (rows 30-44), with the grille slats, headlights and bumper. The top surfaces are large and each part has an edge line, so this is a three-quarter view with a front face of 3+ rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 17 visible tones per full tile, matching the stall (17) and well (20) and above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 2%, close to the references (0-13%). Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted: dark green-teal beside the body, not a black sticker line. By eye the car body has about 5 green steps (highlight, light, mid, dark, deep) plus rust patches, cracked glass lines and grille detail. The roof and hood panels carry some grain and variation, but a few panels are smoother than the reference stall and well, so texture is 'some' rather than 'rich'. Overall it would sit acceptably next to the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: Measured facts are at the reference level: 17 visible tones per tile (stall 17, well 20, hedge 9), 2% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted dark green and not a black sticker line. By eye the car reads as a green body with a darker green outline, rust patches, cracked glass and a grille. Each material ramp is only about 3-4 steps, whereas the references carry 5-6, with the roof and hood panels fairly broad and smooth. Texture is present as rust speckle and crack lines but is sparser than the per-tile scallops, grain and clumps on the stall and well. Overall it is clean and close to the references but slightly thinner in shading depth and grain, and I am not confident a careful artist would accept it as equal, so with doubt it fails.
